encounters.cc: Brought to ED after falling from second-story window during witnessed seizure, intubated for airway protection

lines: Brought to ED after falling from second-story window during witnessed seizure, intubated for airway protection

This 32-year-old female with childhood-onset generalized epilepsy and central diabetes insipidus previously complicated by gestational exacerbation during pregnancy in 2022 presents to the emergency department following a witnessed seizure and fall.
On arrival, she is obtunded and postictal.
Her roommate reports that the patient has had epilepsy since childhood and recently stopped taking her medications.
She is intubated for airway protection.
Over the next two hours, she receives 120 mL of isotonic saline but continues to have profuse urine output, totaling 1.4 liters.
- Diabetes insipidus in pregnancy (gestational exacerbation of central diabetes insipidus) (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
- HIV infection (advanced, CDC Stage 3, diagnosed 3 years prior)
- Laparoscopic salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic pregnancy (age 26)
- Desmopressin acetate 0.1 mg PO twice daily
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis, type 2 diabetes mellitus
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use. Occupation: Graphic designer.
Her temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), pulse is 108/min, and blood pressure is 138/90 mm Hg.
Physical examination reveals irregular respirations and sluggishly reactive pupils.
There is no purposeful movement in response to painful stimuli, and she exhibits decerebrate posturing.
Head CT shows bilateral cerebral contusions and a small intraventricular hemorrhage.

encounters.cc: Several days of worsening occipital headache and new-onset confusion with lethargy

lines: Several days of worsening occipital headache and new-onset confusion with lethargy
This 33-year-old with advanced HIV, epilepsy, and central diabetes insipidus presents with headache and confusion.
The pain is described as dull and located in the occipital region.
She has had difficulty maintaining attention and is increasingly lethargic, per her roommate.
- Diabetes insipidus in pregnancy (gestational exacerbation of central diabetes insipidus) (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
- HIV infection (advanced, CDC Stage 3, diagnosed 3 years prior)
She was diagnosed with HIV 3 years ago but has been poorly adherent to antiretroviral therapy.
- Laparoscopic salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic pregnancy (age 26)
- Desmopressin acetate 0.1 mg PO twice daily
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis, type 2 diabetes mellitus
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use. Occupation: Graphic designer.
She is afebrile, blood pressure is 110/65 mmHg, pulse is 94/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
On examination, she is oriented only to person. Fundoscopy reveals no papilledema.
Her current CD4+ T cell count is 50/µL.
A non-contrast CT scan of the head reveals four ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia and subcortical white matter.

encounters.cc: Brought by roommate after discovery of suicide note with 6-month history of worsening depression and weight loss

lines: Brought by roommate after discovery of suicide note with 6-month history of worsening depression and weight loss

The patient, who has childhood-onset epilepsy, central diabetes insipidus, advanced HIV, and recurrent severe major depressive disorder, presents after her roommate discovered a suicide note, with prior toxoplasmosis and seizures.
The patient admits to writing the note and expresses a desire to end her life due to overwhelming feelings of worthlessness and hopelessness.
She reports a 6-month history of depressed mood, anhedonia, significant weight loss, insomnia, and decreased concentration.
She reveals that she has a detailed plan to overdose on her roommate's prescription medications and has already collected the pills.
- Diabetes insipidus in pregnancy (gestational exacerbation of central diabetes insipidus) (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
- HIV infection (advanced, CDC Stage 3, diagnosed 3 years prior)
She has a history of major depressive disorder.
- Laparoscopic salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic pregnancy (age 26)
She was previously on sertraline, which she stopped taking 3 months ago.
- Desmopressin acetate 0.1 mg PO twice daily
- Prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tablet PO daily
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis, type 2 diabetes mellitus
On examination, she is tearful, has poor eye contact, and speaks in a low, monotone voice. and physical examination is unremarkable.
Laboratory tests, including a complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and thyroid function tests, are within normal limits.
